column1: # Expected permission-gate decision, tab, command text. Both hooks must agree on every line.
# Blank lines and # lines are skipped. An empty command stands for a tool call with no command field.
# The token <NL> stands for a newline, which lets a case carry a heredoc.
# git writes are the user's alone
# Staging under another name, and the Windows executable spelling
# Rewrites of history or the working tree
# The read half of a verb that names both a read and a write
# A flag that only shapes the listing acts on a name or write flag after it
# apply stops at the working tree until a flag hands it the index

column2: git apply patch.diff && git commit -m x
git apply patch.diff; git apply --index other.diff

column1: # A worktree writes refs and metadata into the user's .git, so only its listing is a read

column2: git worktree add ../wt && git commit -m x
git commit -m x; git worktree add ../wt

column1: # The boundary is a word edge, not a delimiter list, so quoting and paths do not smuggle a write
# A gated name inside a longer word is not an invocation
# sudo named in quoted data is no call, unless the quotes reach a shell
# An inline interpreter script that writes files skips the Edit and Write hooks
# Backgrounding from inside the shell, which run_in_background does where the harness can see it
# An ampersand that redirects, chains, calls or belongs to an argument is not backgrounding

column2: unzip $(gh run download 1 --dir out; echo out)/a.zip

column1: # An explicit read method makes field flags read-only again
# Driving CI is a write, but destroys nothing durable

column2: gh workflow run ci.yml --ref main -f env=prod

column1: # gh writes, including the glued flag form and the unmethoded field flag

column2: gh api -X GET repos/o/r -X DELETE repos/o/r

column1: # graphql cannot be told apart from a mutation without reading the query body
# Every gh invocation in the command has to pass

column2: gh run download 1 && gh pr merge 5
gh run view $(gh run list -L1 --json databaseId -q '.[0].databaseId')

column1: # Program names fold case, as on the macOS and Windows filesystems that resolve them
# Subcommands and flags keep their case, as git and gh read them, so an uppercase one runs nothing
# SSH key material, in every path spelling: no settings.json rule covers this one
# A file merely named for ssh is not the key directory, and reaching a host exposes no key
# The client config and host list name hosts and options, never keys
# A config key given no value is read back, and a value sets it

column2: git config core.autocrlf && git commit -m x
git config core.autocrlf; git config core.editor vim

column1: # Only options stand between git and its subcommand, so a verb used as a name is not the subcommand
# gh named without a subcommand, or asked for its version
# A job the same command waits for cannot outlive the call
# An ampersand inside a quoted string is data, unless the string is handed to a shell as its command
# A heredoc body fed to a reader or an interpreter is text, not the command

column2: cat > notes.md <<'EOF'<NL>Run sudo apt-get install, then gh pr merge, then read ~/.ssh/id_rsa<NL>EOF

column1: # A heredoc body fed to a shell, or left unclosed, stays in view
# An unquoted delimiter runs each command substitution in the body, so those lines stay in view

column2: cat > notes.md <<EOF<NL>Built at $(date)<NL>Run git push after review<NL>EOF

column1: # A scratch clone under .agent/git/ named by -C takes every local write, but never a push
# A clone creates a new repository and leaves the user's untouched, wherever it lands

column2: git -C .agent/git/r fetch origin pull/123/head:pr-123 && git -C .agent/git/r switch pr-123

column1: # Quoted text is data unless it runs: a pattern or message naming a write verb is no call
# A quoted value handed to a git option keeps the subcommand after it in view
# Quoted text that executes stays in view
# An rm target with an unguarded variable trips Claude Code's root-removal prompt, which no hook clears

column2: W=$(mktemp -d); for t in a b; do rm -f "${W:?}/${t:?}"; done
git rev-parse HEAD; npm run format-rm
W=$(mktemp -d); for t in a b; do rm -f $W/$t; done
